title: Pointwise fibre dimension is additive for a flat first morphism
statement: Let $a:U\to X$ and $f:X\to S$ be locally finite type morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $u\in U$, $x=a(u)$ and $s=f(x)$. Assume $a$ is flat at $u$ [def-weil-flat-morphism]. For the scheme-theoretic fibres $U_s$ of $f\circ a$, $U_x$ of $a$, and $X_s$ of $f$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre], their dimensions at the indicated points [def-kun-dimension] satisfy $\dim_u(U_s)=\dim_u(U_x)+\dim_x(X_s)$.

source.place: Tag 02JS (lemma-dimension-fibre-at-a-point-additive), equality when the first morphism is flat at the indicated point

proof.text: Use [lem-sbc-composite-fibre-local-models] to write $A=\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$, $B=\mathcal O_{U_s,u}$, $C=\mathcal O_{U_x,u}$. The rings are Noetherian local; the map $A\to B$ is local and flat since $a$ is flat at $u$, and $B/\mathfrak m_A B\cong C$. The lemma also supplies finite-type affine neighbourhoods in all three fibres, with the same stalks and residue fields as the original points. No Noetherian hypothesis on $S$ is required.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula] to the flat map $A\to B$ at the maximal ideal of $B$. Locality makes its contraction the maximal ideal of $A$; localization at either maximal ideal changes nothing. Its equality therefore reads $\dim B=\dim A+\dim(B/\mathfrak m_A B)=\dim A+\dim C$, where the last equality uses the closed-fibre isomorphism of Step 1.

Apply [lem-kun-dimension-formula] to the three finite-type affine neighbourhoods from Step 1. The stalk and residue identifications there give $\dim_u U_s=\dim B+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(u)$, $\dim_u U_x=\dim C+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(x)}\kappa(u)$, and $\dim_x X_s=\dim A+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(x)$. The passage from the affine neighbourhood to the whole fibre uses [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace], which states equality of dimension at the point for an open subspace. Apply [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] on each finite-type affine neighbourhood: its global dimension is finite, hence its dimension at the point is finite by the defining minimum over neighbourhoods. The displayed formulas consequently have finite nonnegative local-ring and transcendence-degree terms.

Use [lem-sbc-transcendence-degree-tower] for the compatible field maps $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(x)\to\kappa(u)$: $t_{su}=t_{xu}+t_{sx}$. Substituting this and $\dim B=\dim A+\dim C$ into Step 3 gives $\dim_u U_s=\dim A+\dim C+t_{xu}+t_{sx}=(\dim C+t_{xu})+(\dim A+t_{sx})=\dim_u U_x+\dim_x X_s$. All terms here are finite because the three neighbourhoods are finite type over fields; equivalently one can add the displayed formulas in extended dimensions, with no subtraction or cancellation.
